changes: The document-authoritative TheoryDeveloper can now choose checkpoint_theory_progress after writing substantive Markdown/LaTeX, preserve the exact file manifest and compact handoff state, and continue under the same TheoryDeveloper owner without Architect routing or content repair.

AgentRuntime stores partial theory state once as a content-addressed blackboard artifact and passes only a RuntimeArtifactRef to the continuation task. Partial progress remains accepted=false, kernel_verified=false, and supplies no theory, empirical, formal, or proof credit.

Initial continuation is rebound to the exact original question, prompt mode, and compact Architect context; targeted revision continuation remains bound to the exact reviewer lineage. Missing, changed, or hash-mismatched files and stale context fail before a model call.

The existing TheoryDeveloper workspace now exposes one no-input run_research_source action for an operator-fixed, hash-bound paper entrypoint and environment. The same model reads raw stdout and stderr; it cannot choose the command, edit source, inherit secrets, or use network access.

Explicit task_intent can terminate a source-replication-only objective with one model-authored Markdown report and gap checkpoint without fabricating theory, generated code, simulation, novelty, or formal proof artifacts.

Evaluator-only source replication gold runs after AgentRuntime termination. It validates immutable source, environment, stdout, and hidden numeric identity without entering model context or generating runtime feedback.

Research-eval CLI completion now follows the frozen gold scoring scope: component gold does not require unrelated research lanes, while full_task gold still requires the complete research loop inside the evaluator.

After fresh L1 exposed an inconsistent turn/tool bound, source-only workspaces were changed so max turns can reach the already-authorized tool-call count. This adds no tool call, retry, agent, scheduler, content patch, task-family answer, or model tier escalation.
Not-applicable evidence dimensions no longer claim gold_validated merely because their evaluator lane was skipped.

Hash-bound source search now exposes the best non-overlapping result from distinct documents before filling remaining slots with additional ranges. This prevents one long paper from crowding an exact definition or implementation out of a small top-k without adding a source router or task-family rule.

TheoryDeveloper source guidance now asks the same model to inspect the most specific primary definition or implementation for model-, score-, or implementation-specific claims and to separate exact execution facts from unsupported interpretation.

AgentRuntime and serious TheoryDeveloper authoring now fail closed when the backend lacks native client-tool turns instead of silently switching mathematical authority back to a regenerated JSON packet. A recovered interface-stage checkpoint is accepted only when its core is already bound to model-authored Markdown/LaTeX documents.

Explicit per-question task intent now owns mandatory outer-graph evidence: required dimensions remain fail-closed, not_applicable dimensions cannot be resurrected by stale feedback or Architect routing, and optional dimensions may be selected by the Architect without becoming completion gates.

TheoryDeveloper keeps Markdown/LaTeX documents as mathematical authority while its compact JSON handoff now requires only the estimator, simulation, theorem, proof-plan, and formalization ABIs needed by that question.
Research-evaluation completion and the terminal Critic now apply the same required, optional, and not_applicable evidence vector instead of one global theory-code-simulation-formal pipeline.

Canonical AgentRuntime now removes provider/tool transcript history from the persisted Theory packet and stores it once as a separate evidence artifact bound to the exact packet ID and content hash. Critic source-grounding audit resolves that evidence without making mathematical identity depend on transport history; legacy direct packets remain readable.

The existing document-authoritative claim index now records model-authored direct dependency edges between stable claim IDs. Runtime validates only graph closure and acyclicity, while AlgorithmEngineer, SimulationEvaluator, Formalizer, and independent theory preflight consume the same dependency graph alongside the same hash-bound Markdown/LaTeX documents.

Every document-authoritative Theory revision now emits one compact content-addressed delta over claim IDs, statuses, direct dependencies, anchors, and document hashes. It copies no mathematical body. Independent preflight sees the immediate delta, while terminal Critic reconstructs the exact multi-revision chain and rejects a delta whose fingerprint or packet hashes do not match.

TheoryDeveloper revision bindings now persist one standard RuntimeArtifactRef to the exact parent Theory packet instead of recursively copying its semantic body. AgentRuntime resolves that reference only inside the selected TheoryDeveloper call, rejects missing or stale bytes before any model call, and removes the hydrated material before the next task or resumable continuation. The legacy prior-material context path and dual embedded/reference binding shapes were deleted.

The same TheoryDeveloper client-tool session can now search current Markdown/LaTeX/BibTeX documents by model-chosen literal text and read exact inclusive line ranges bound to the current document SHA-256. This removes the prior failure mode where a document larger than the whole-observation limit became unreadable. Search/read bodies remain visible to the active model but persisted workspace evidence stores only hash-bound inspection references.

Independent theory preflight now uses those same two generic document tools instead of serializing every authoritative Markdown/LaTeX file into one JSON prompt or searching a truncated document row. The reviewing model chooses the claims, queries, and line ranges; at least one exact read is required before it signs a review when file authority exists. Runtime records only source-packet-bound document hashes and line-range hashes, redacts document bodies from persisted tool history, and keeps external RAG search separate from inspection of the candidate itself.

Evaluator-only source replication now separates immutable source/environment/output identity from the model-authored report's scientific interpretation. An optional calibrated exact-Haiku document judge can score the hash-bound report only after runtime termination; calibration failure, report mutation, or missing source identity fails closed and cannot generate runtime feedback.

Document-authoritative Theory packets no longer acquire empty legacy derivation_steps, equation_chain, assumption_ledger, or sanity_checks arrays during normalization. Markdown/LaTeX remains the mathematical authority; JSON retains only the claim and sanity-check index plus downstream estimator, theorem, simulation, proof-plan, and optional formalization handoffs.

The model-visible question hash now includes explicit task intent, and evaluator preflight rejects any mismatch between visible and hidden source, theory, code, empirical, formal, novelty, or unresolved-gap requirements before a model call. Evidence scope can no longer drift while retaining the same visible-question identity.

Canonical TheoryDeveloper authoring now separates one strict model-owned path-plus-content Markdown/LaTeX/BibTeX write from the small structured claim-index and executable-ABI handoff. The runtime stores and validates exact bytes but neither interprets nor repairs the mathematics; the former batch document_writes input remains compatibility-only and is no longer exposed to the model.

Theory-only hidden evaluation now counts as a genuinely evaluated gold task even when no algorithm harness is configured, while every not-applicable dimension reports not_configured authority instead of naming a hidden evaluator that never ran.

TheoryDeveloper initial and revision prompts now describe the actual direct-document, hash-bound edit, and structured-handoff tools instead of instructing the model to use the removed combined batch shape. The executor no longer accepts document_writes through write_theory_workspace, and deterministic replay proves the same model receives a direct-tool correction rather than a runtime content patch.

Canonical scripted theory sessions now write one complete mathematical document and one mutually consistent structured handoff instead of splitting the handoff into arbitrary two-artifact batches. This reduced the representative initial session from eight to six tool turns and from five to three accepted writes without increasing any budget.
